newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vol rises in nervous pre-FOMC trade.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vol rises in nervous pre-FOMC trade.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE was pushed higher on Tuesday by a combination of concerns about a possible U.S. rate rise and prospects for European economic and monetary union (EMU), traders in London said.

The results of the meeting of U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, the policy making arm of the Federal Reserve, is expected after 1800 GMT. Opinion is divided over whether interest rates will be raised, and if they are, by how much.

Also, traders said there are still concerns that Germany's plan announced last week to revalue its gold reserves suggested that a relaxed attitude to accounting in order to meet EMU criteria would be allowed.
"Worries about a soft euro have been niggling for a while, and with the FOMC as well today, volatility got a boost," said a trader at a major British brokerage in London.

June options on the June Bund futures expire on Thursday, and activity was focused on closing out positions. A major U.S. brokerage was selling 101.00 strike June puts, and traders said about 14,000 lots had gone through over the last few days.
"There are a lot of gamma trades," said the British brokerage trader.
Gamma is the measure of the rate of change in the delta of the underlying asset price.

July options on the September futures were trading at a volatility of 5.7 percent, up from 5.55 percent on Monday. September futures were down 0.03 at 100.56 by 1500 GMT. June futures were up 10 basis points at 101.64.
"The FOMC could go either way," said Luke White, a broker at Fimat Futures in London. "The rise in the CRB index might be something that could tip the balance."

The Commodity Research Bureau index was at 252.52 on Tuesday, compared with 239.98 in April. Traders said the Fed's desire to be seen as preemptive, rather than reactive, could mean the rise in the CRB was a possible justification for a rate hike. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
